title: One Number Decides! Discriminant Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Three equations that look almost the same: x² - 6x + 5, x² - 6x + 9 and x² - 6x + 13. One has two different real roots, one has a single repeated root, and one has no real root at all. Can you tell which is which without solving? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 4, Complex Numbers and Quadratic Equations) one small number does it for you: the discriminant D = b² - 4ac.

You will watch D fall from 16 to -16 as c counts up, while the curve cuts the axis twice, touches it once, then lifts off and its roots step onto the Argand plane as a complex pair. We prove in four steps why the sign of D decides everything, split D > 0 into rational and irrational roots, find k for equal roots with a live slider, and fix the exam trap of D > 0 versus D ≥ 0. Two pause-and-think questions, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Note: the discriminant appears in the Class 10 NCERT text; in Class 11 it is part of the JEE Main syllabus but not of the current rationalised NCERT text.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.
